svg.aria-label: Carrier board PCB floorplan, 27 x 27 mm
svg.text: LIFCL-40 CrossLink-NX + AR0234CS machine-vision camera. The carrier sits behind TIDA-010083 in the same 27 × 27 mm envelope and inside a 29 mm housing.
Placement is driven by three things in this order: the FPGA bank voltages, the thermal path out of the FPGA, and the distance from the switching node to the image sensor.
component side · faces the TIDA board
X-ray view — same coordinate frame, not mirrored
One cable in. Everything inside is a shielded volume
with exactly one DC ground bond.
WHY THE PARTS SIT WHERE THEY DO
289-csBGA, 9.5 × 9.5 mm, 0.5 mm pitch. Rotated so bank 1 faces
the TIDA connector and the D-PHY quad faces the sensor FPC.
96-ball FBGA on the east flank. Single rank, point-to-point,
every net under 25 mm — no fly-by, no VTT island.
22 signals, 6 × 5 V contacts for 2.3 A, 20 grounds. Pinout in
5 MIPI pairs with a ground between each, I²C, RESET, EXTCLK,
TRIGGER, FLASH, and two power feeds.
Local reference for the DDR3L PLL. CLK_OUT from the PHY drives
0.5 pF ESD array on the low-speed flex lines, at the
5 V input bulk for the point-of-load zone.
8 × 8 mm mask-free copper, 64 vias of Ø0.30 mm, filled and
capped. The only conduction path out of a fanless csBGA.
0201s just outside the ball shadow. The BGA shadow is thermal
land, so the thin L1–L2 dielectric carries the high-frequency
1.0 V, 1.8 V, 1.35 V, 1.2 V. Farthest corner from the sensor
FPC. Local island, stitched on all four sides.
Pads only, no connector, no board area spent on a header.
Ferrite + cap on every rail entering the sensor flex, at the
Bank 1 is 2.5 V for RGMII, bank 4 is 1.35 V for DDR3L, bank 5
is 1.8 V for the sensor. Those three banks cannot be
re-ordered, so the package orientation is fixed before a
The switcher is the loudest thing on the board.
4 MHz point-of-load converters sit in the corner diagonally
opposite the sensor flex. Distance costs nothing here and buys
sensor-row noise margin that no filter recovers later.
Heat leaves through the board, not the air.
No fan, a sealed housing, and a sensor whose dark current
roughly doubles every 6–8 °C. The bottom-side land under the
FPGA is reserved before any passive is placed.
MIPI is short because it is placed short.
The D-PHY escape faces the FPC and the gap is 2.4 mm. Nothing
crosses it — no rail, no plane split, no serpentine.
The connector footprints are the immovable objects.
They are set by the TIDA board above and the lens mount in
front. Everything else was placed around them.
